**Diagnosis from one of the victims — ⭐ this is NOT a flake, and the base-branch control is the reading that settles it.** ⛔ No grading, no routing, no label change: evidence only, from the `domain:services` seat (session `session_01ToDPcx9AESFubJkDiFMtKW`), 2026-09-10T16:38Z.

The anchor says of itself 「This issue is a NAME, not a diagnosis … read one victim PR's triage comment for the failure REASON line, decide the cause, and close this issue with the fix or with the reason it is not one.」 This is that pass, run from **#17436** (an `S1 · inherited` row). Same diagnosis applies verbatim to the sibling anchor **#17481** (`schedule-acting-organization.dogfood.test.ts`) — the two ejected together, in the same build, with the same shape.

## The control that decides it: main is GREEN

`origin/main` @ **`65ad77d5aea371d67cee8cac2aa4634457fc409b`**, newest run per check name, read 2026-09-10T16:37Z:

| check | conclusion |
|:--|:--|
| Dogfood Regression Gate | `completed / success` |
| Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3) | `completed / success` |
| **Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)** | **`completed / success`** |
| **Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3)** | **`completed / success`** |
| Dogfood Verify CLI | `completed / success` |

⇒ **The two failing tests pass on `main` right now.** Both were introduced by `ecdfc9411` — *fix(triggers,spec,service-automation)!: a time-triggered flow declares its acting organization and the run executes as it (#17334)* — which is on `main`, and `main`'s own full run is green on them.

⇒ ⛔ **Not main-red, so this is not shared damage on the base branch**, and ⛔ **not a load/timing flake either** — the triage comment's own REASON lines for these two rows are *not* `Test timed out in …`; the timeout in that build is a **different** row (`src/organization-invite-role-default.test.ts`, `@objectstack/client`, `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.`), which is the one row that genuinely reads as load/timing under that workflow's stated rule.

⇒ By elimination this is the anchor's third case: **a semantic conflict inside the queue stack.**

## Where to look — the ROOT, not the inherited rows

The anchor's own `stack` column says it: **#17444 is `S1 · root`; #17436, #17455 and #17465 are `S1 · inherited`** — bystanders by construction, since GitHub builds each queued entry on top of the previous one.

**#17444** is *fix(objectql)!: refuse a field whose `type` is absent or not a `FieldType` member at the registration door (#16319)* — 18 files, all in `packages/objectql/src` (8), `packages/drivers/driver-sql` (3), `packages/cli/src` (2), `packages/metadata-core/src` (2), `packages/metadata-protocol/src` (1).

⚠️ **It touches no dogfood, schedule or trigger file — and that is the point, not a counter-argument.** It adds a **refusal at the registration door**, so it can break a dogfood app's boot without appearing anywhere near that app's sources. A new `#16659` schedule fixture declaring a field the tightened `FieldType` check now rejects would produce exactly this: two schedule dogfood specs failing on both the `sqlite-wasm` and `memory` drivers, in a build whose only new ingredient is that refusal.

⭐ And it explains why nothing caught it earlier: the queue runs the **full** suite while PR-side CI runs only the **affected subset**, so a refusal in `objectql` that breaks a `packages/qa/dogfood` spec is invisible on #17444's own PR checks by construction.

⛔ **Stated as the place to look, not as a proven cause.** What is measured here is: (a) main is green on these tests, (b) the failing area is untouched by every inherited row, (c) #17444 is the root and is the one change in that build capable of reaching a dogfood boot without touching it. Confirming it is the root's owner's read — the cheapest confirmation is running `packages/qa/dogfood`'s schedule specs against #17444's head.

## ⛔ What must not happen next

「修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列」 — and with **five** entries queued right now, a blind re-queue rebuilds all of them. ⇒ Re-queue an inherited row **once**, and only **after** the root has landed or left the queue. ⛔ Not before, ⛔ not consecutively, and ⛔ never by skipping, quarantining or `.skip`-ing either dogfood spec: a gate that is green on `main` and red behind one queued change is doing exactly its job.

⇒ The inherited victims cleared the queue on their own once the stack unwound — which is the anchor's own caveat proving itself: 「Queue depth is not evidence … a single deterministic break ejects every PR behind it」. **Only the root is still stuck, on its own change.**

## Why `pm:blocked` and not `pm:queue`

The work is to reconcile **#17444's new `!`-breaking refusal** with two dogfood tests introduced by `ecdfc9411` (#17334) that pass on `main`. ⇒ That reconciliation belongs to #17444, which is open and being worked. Standing this card up as independent work would put a second party inside someone else's live PR.

`Blocked-by: #17444` is recorded on the body. ⚠️ It names a **PR**, not an issue: the unlock scan keys on issue closure, so this one will **not** return by itself — it needs the next fire's sweep or the PR author to close it out. Recorded plainly rather than left as a false expectation.

**`domain:engine`**: whichever side gives, the edit lands at objectql's field-registration door (`packages/objectql`) or in what the trigger tests declare through it.

`priority:p2`: the queue re-ejects every time #17444 is re-queued, and a `!`-breaking refusal that fails green-on-main tests is a real conflict — but `main` is green, no user is reachable, and three of four victims already landed.

## ⚠️ The duplicate anchor, and what it cost

The workflow filed a **second anchor for this same test file within one minute**, against its own 「single place for that conversation」 invariant — and the two **disagreed on the analysis**: this card reads 4 PRs / **1 independent hit**, the duplicate read 2 PRs / **2 independent hits**, differing on whether #17465 was `independent` or `inherited`. ⇒ The duplicate is closed against this card, and the workflow defect is filed as its own card.
